planting.note: Set bulbs or green divisions 3-4 inches deep in cool, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade under deciduous cover.

directions: Set bulbs or green divisions 3 to 4 inches deep in cool, humus-rich soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs where partial to full shade prevails through the growing season. Ailwyn is one of the lesser-known snowdrop selections carrying the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, valued by collectors for dependable vigor and a clean, well-proportioned flower shape rather than any single flashy trait. Keep the site undisturbed and evenly moist from autumn through spring, letting foliage yellow and die back naturally before any division. Lift and replant congested colonies right after flowering while leaves are still green to keep bloom counts strong.
sources: Bishop, Davis & Grimshaw, Snowdrops: A Monograph of Cultivated Galanthus

common_name: Bertram Anderson Snowdrop (Lower Slaughter Historic Snowdrop)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant bulbs in fall, 3 to 4 inches deep, in moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in the same partial-to-full-shade woodland-edge conditions favored by most garden snowdrops. Named for Gloucestershire plantsman and noted galanthophile Bertram Anderson, who gardened at Lower Slaughter and championed many alpine and shade perennials still grown today, this selection reflects his eye for robust, garden-worthy forms. It builds into healthy clumps steadily when left undisturbed in cool ground topped yearly with leaf mold. Divide and replant overcrowded clumps right after the flowers fade while the foliage is still green.
sources: Bishop, Davis & Grimshaw, Snowdrops: A Monograph of Cultivated Galanthus

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil beneath deciduous trees or shrubs where shade is partial to full through summer. Comet holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit among the roster of long-cultivated snowdrop selections prized by collectors for reliable increase and garden performance rather than rarity alone. Leave clumps undisturbed to bulk up over several seasons, mulching lightly with leaf mold each autumn. Lift and separate crowded clumps immediately after bloom while foliage remains green for the best re-establishment.
sources: Bishop, Davis & Grimshaw, Snowdrops: A Monograph of Cultivated Galanthus

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in cool, moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in cool, moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, ideally naturalized under deciduous trees where the ground stays undisturbed year to year. John Gray is among the historic snowdrop cultivars carrying the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, grown chiefly by collectors building a representative spread of named forms. It increases at a typical pace for garden snowdrops and tolerates being left in place for many years without division. Divide only when clumps become congested, lifting right after flowering while the leaves are still green.
sources: Bishop, Davis & Grimshaw, Snowdrops: A Monograph of Cultivated Galanthus

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in partial to full shade, the same cool woodland conditions suited to other historic snowdrop cultivars. Merlin carries a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit and is often described by galanthophiles as having an unusually solid, dark-marked inner segment rather than the thin V-shaped mark typical of wild snowdrop populations. Grow it in an undisturbed spot where it can bulk up gradually into a dense clump over several seasons. Divide congested clumps right after flowering while foliage is still green to keep the display vigorous.
sources: Bishop, Davis & Grimshaw, Snowdrops: A Monograph of Cultivated Galanthus

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in cool, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in cool, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade beneath deciduous trees or shrubs. Trumps is an inverse poculiform selection raised by English galanthophile Richard Hobbs, notable because its inner segments expand nearly as large as the outer ones, giving each flower an open, star-shaped look quite unlike the typical bell-in-skirt snowdrop form. It is grown mainly by specialist collectors who value the unusual flower architecture over rapid increase. Divide clumps sparingly, right after bloom while leaves remain green, since this form tends to multiply more slowly than common garden snowdrops.
sources: Bishop, Davis & Grimshaw, Snowdrops: A Monograph of Cultivated Galanthus

common_name: Spring Fling Bergenia (Terra Nova Pink Pigsqueak)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and mulch lightly each spring to keep the leathery rounded leaves lush and weed pressure down. Spring Fling is a Terra Nova Nurseries bergenia bred for an especially profuse early-spring flush of pink flower clusters held above the clumping evergreen foliage, which takes on bronze-red tones through winter cold. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and spreads gradually by thick rhizomes, making it a dependable textural anchor for shaded borders and woodland edges. Divide congested clumps every four to five years in spring just as new growth begins.

common_name: Angel Kiss Dragonfly Bergenia (Compact Pink Pigsqueak)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade, topping the bed with compost each spring to keep the glossy, rounded foliage vigorous. Angel Kiss belongs to Terra Nova Nurseries' Dragonfly series of compact bergenias, bred for soft pink flower clusters on a smaller-statured plant than species forms, suiting shaded rock gardens and container plantings. The leathery evergreen leaves flush purple-red in winter, adding color after the bloom has passed. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and spreads slowly by rhizome; divide congested clumps every four to five years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Site in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where the clumping, leathery foliage stays lush through the growing season. Early Brilliance Magenta is a Terra Nova Nurseries selection bred to open its vivid magenta-pink flower clusters ahead of most other bergenias in spring, giving an earlier burst of color in a shaded bed. Foliage deepens to bronze-purple through winter, carrying the planting's interest past the bloom period. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and increases steadily by rhizome; divide crowded clumps every four to five years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade, and refresh the surrounding mulch each spring to support the rounded, leathery foliage. Vintage Blush is part of Terra Nova Nurseries' Vintage series of bergenias, chosen for soft, pale pink flower clusters that read as a gentler complement to the deeper rose tones of other series members. Its evergreen leaves take on warm bronze shading in winter cold, extending the plant's garden value beyond the spring bloom. Clumps spread gradually by rhizome and are deer- and rabbit-resistant; divide every four to five years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, dividing and top-dressing clumps periodically to keep foliage dense. Vintage Bouquet is a Terra Nova Nurseries bergenia in the Vintage series, selected for an especially full, many-stemmed cluster of pink flowers that reads as a bouquet-like show above the rounded evergreen leaves each spring. Winter cold turns the leathery foliage shades of bronze and red, giving the planting a second season of interest. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and spreads slowly by rhizome; divide congested clumps every four to five years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, mulching annually to protect the shallow rhizomes through winter freeze-thaw cycles. Vintage Pink anchors Terra Nova Nurseries' Vintage series with a clear, medium-pink flower cluster held above bold, leathery leaves that bronze attractively once cold weather sets in. It forms dense, weed-smothering clumps over time and tolerates heavier shade than most flowering shade perennials. Being deer- and rabbit-resistant, it suits naturalistic shaded borders; divide crowded clumps every four to five years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring with the crown at soil level, in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Site in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, dividing established clumps every few years to keep the stand vigorous. Vintage Rose is the deepest-toned member of Terra Nova Nurseries' Vintage bergenia series, carrying rose-pink flower clusters on sturdy stems above rounded, leathery foliage that colors bronze-red in winter. Its clumping habit and tolerance of fairly deep shade make it a reliable front-of-border choice beneath deciduous shrubs. Deer- and rabbit-resistant and slow to spread by rhizome, it needs little upkeep beyond an annual spring mulch and division of overcrowded clumps every four to five years.
